assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

The scenario asserts the smallest tool-less round trip: `ready → working → ready`, final state `ready`, zero tool calls, regardless of which adapter-specific signal closes the turn.

**Muse's end signal is its `terminal` event on the run stream.** Every prompt Muse handles opens with `payload_type:"runtime.session", payload.kind:"run", event.kind:"started"` (carries the literal prompt) and closes with `event.kind:"terminal"` (a `terminal` field discriminating `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`, format-spec §3, 37 real samples: 31 completed, 5 cancelled, 1 failed). `parser.go`'s `parseRunTerminal` (parser.go:324-365) sets `EventType="turn_done"` for ALL THREE outcomes — the run objectively ended in every case, the SessionError-vs-ready branch is what the classifier does with that, not a different EventType. This is directly unit-tested: `TestParseLine_RunTerminal_Completed_TurnDone` (parser_test.go:100-111) asserts `EventType=="turn_done"` and `SessionError==nil` on a `terminal:"completed"` record, and `TestParseLine_TurnCompleted_RealFixture` (parser_test.go:596-610) replays a real, redacted captured turn (testdata/real-turn-completed.jsonl) end-to-end through `tailer.NewTranscriptTailer(...).TailAndProcess()` and asserts `LastEventType=="turn_done"`, `HasOpenToolCall==false`, `SessionError==nil`, nonzero cumulative tokens — i.e. the exact mechanism this scenario needs is already green under `go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/... -race -count=1` (ran it: all tests pass).

**Tool-less is structural, not incidental.** `ToolUses`/`HasOpenToolCall` are populated ONLY by `parseAssistantToolCallsCommitted` reacting to an `assistant_tool_calls_committed` record (parser.go:445-463); a turn whose assistant reply never calls a tool never touches that path, so `HasOpenToolCall` stays false by construction and can never veto `IsAgentDone()`.

**Classifier mechanism (shared, adapter-agnostic — already covered by its own tests, cited not re-verified here).** `SessionMetrics.IsAgentDone()` (core/domain/session/metrics.go:569-599): `HasOpenToolCall`/`HasLiveBackgroundProcess` veto false; else `HookTurnDone` (muse declares no hooks — agent.go's doc — so this is always false for muse) `|| LastEventType=="turn_done"` (metrics.go:599, the path muse's transcript tier feeds). `state_classifier.go`'s `classifyAgentDone` (state_classifier.go:399-452): a `SessionError` routes to `error`; `metrics.IsWaitingForUserInput()` (line 436) routes to `waiting`; otherwise `transitionTo(..., session.StateReady, "agent finished turn → ready")` (line 452) — rule 2b, working→ready.

**The waiting branch is fed correctly too**, which matters for the scenario's negative invariant (a tool-less reply must not accidentally divert to `waiting`). `parseAssistantMessageCommitted` (parser.go:428-439) sets `ev.PendingWaitingCue = session.ProseIndicatesWaiting(tailer.WaitingScanWindow(text))` over the FULL assistant text (not the truncated display tail, matching every other adapter's #1150 fix) on every `assistant_message_committed` record — confirmed unit-tested by `TestParseLine_AssistantMessageCommitted_WaitingCue`/`_EmptyTextNoWaitingCue` (parser_test.go:245-264). A recipe whose final reply is a plain declarative sentence (no trailing question, no imperative "let me know"/"verify and reply" cue — `session.ProseIndicatesWaiting`, waiting_cue.go:29-33) never sets this flag, so `classifyAgentDone` falls through past the waiting branch straight to `ready`.

**Session identity / birth shape — the one genuinely uncertain part, flagged honestly.** Muse is `FilesUnderRoot` with a static `Dir` and `SessionIDFromPath` deriving the id from the session directory's basename (adapter.go:145-159) — a stable UUID once the directory exists. BUT the interactive driver's own launch-seam comment (replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh:207-212) states plainly that "the session dir may only materialize after the first prompt lands" — i.e. at `muse --trust-workspace` launch there is no `session.jsonl` yet, only the running `muse-bin-*` process. Read against `core/cmd/irrlichd/wiring.go:103-114` (`buildAgentWatchers`), which unconditionally wires a `processlifecycle.Scanner` for EVERY adapter (muse's `Process.Match` is a `CommandPattern` on `muse-bin-[^/\s]+`, agent.go:65) independent of the `FilesUnderRoot` fswatcher: the scanner will very likely find the running process and mint a `proc-<PID>` pre-session (scanner.go's `HasRealSessionForPID`/`sessionChecker`) before the fswatcher can discover a session.jsonl that doesn't exist yet — the same presession shape codex/gemini-cli/mistral-vibe/pi already exhibit for an analogous reason. This is NOT live-confirmed (no muse recording exists yet), so the spec below is written the same defensively-robust way `pi`'s own `turn-end-terminal-text` cell is (replaydata/agents/pi/scenarios/2-13_turn-end-terminal-text/expected.jsonl): `session_birth` is left UNPINNED to a particular session (matches whichever — presession or real — appears first, born ready), while the turn arc (`turn_start`/`turn_end_terminal`/`pid_bind`/`teardown`) anchors via `same_session_as: turn_start`, and `turn_start` itself is unpinned so the matcher picks the FIRST session to go `working` anywhere in the recording — which structurally must be the real session, since a `proc-<PID>` pre-session never processes a turn and so never goes `working`. This makes the spec correct under EITHER outcome (single real-session birth, or a transient presession that gets superseded), rather than gambling on an unverified guess and risking the exact "collapsed single birth" miss the assess playbook warns produces a PARTIAL. `record` should confirm which shape actually occurs and backflow-correct this note if presession fires.

**Driver.** `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh`'s `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean"` (line 139) covers every primitive this recipe needs (`send`, `wait_turn`, `sleep`) — no `driver=gap`. The three critical defects a prior live audit found (untrusted-workspace modal swallowing the first prompt, a dropped Enter with no inter-keystroke delay, and `resolve_transcript` recursing into a subagent's own transcript) are all fixed in the driver file as it stands on this branch (commit 0239a1bd, "fix(muse): repair the recording driver so it can't record a corrupted pass") — confirmed by reading the current file: `--trust-workspace` is passed at launch (line 235), `step_send` has the `sleep 0.3` between the literal text and Enter (line 349), and `resolve_transcript`'s `find` carries `-not -path '*/subagent/*'` (line 301).
caveats: Vacuous-pass check: this cell would pass while proving nothing if the driven prompt is phrased loosely enough that Muse decides to call a tool anyway (e.g. to "verify" the answer) — the recipe below pins a literal, declarative, tool-free instruction ("Do not use any tools. Reply with exactly this sentence...") for exactly this reason, matching the pattern copilot's and codex's sibling cells already use for the same risk.

Session-birth shape (presession vs. single birth) is inferred from code (wiring.go's unconditional per-adapter process scanner + the driver's own "session dir may only materialize after the first prompt lands" comment) but has NOT been live-confirmed by an actual recording — the spec is deliberately written to be correct either way (pi-pattern), and `record` should backflow-correct this note once it observes the real shape.

cost_nonzero is asserted false, not true: `core/pkg/capacity` has no alias/pricing entry for any `muse-spark-*` model (grepped `core/pkg/capacity/*.go` for "muse" — zero hits), so `EstimatedCostUSD` will very likely compute to $0 even though tokens are genuinely nonzero and durably persisted (format-spec §6: `model_completed.usage`, 476 real records with nonzero usage in the corpus). This is a pricing-catalog gap, not a daemon defect — asserting cost_nonzero:true here would be testing the catalog, not this scenario.

terminal:"cancelled" (the third outcome parseRunTerminal handles) is UNVERIFIED as a human-ESC signal vs. programmatic cancellation (format-spec §3) — irrelevant to this cell, which only exercises terminal:"completed", but noted since parseRunTerminal's cancelled branch is adjacent code this cell's own test coverage does not exercise.

Muse spawns goal-reminder/verify-reminder subagents even for a single simple prompt (format-spec §9) — these are separate ParentSessionID-linked child sessions (confirmed structurally: sessionIDFromPath/parentSessionIDFromPath, adapter.go, mint a distinct id for every subagent's own directory) and do not feed events into the parent session's own state, so they should not perturb this cell's parent-session arc; not live-confirmed for lack of a recording.

LIVE-CONFIRMED (record pass, #1960, recording 2026-09-14-04-36-35, session 01a09dc6-05b5-7711-843f-3a725938ff43): the real session is born directly into ready (single-birth, matches claudecode/aider/junie pattern) with a transient proc-<PID> presession appearing ~400-600ms later and immediately superseded -- resolves the birth-shape ambiguity this assessment flagged as unconfirmed. The recording ALSO exposed a genuine vacuous-pass bug in the ORIGINAL expected.jsonl: turn_start was left unpinned on the assumption that 'the first session to go working anywhere must be the real session', but muse's goal-reminder/verify-reminder subagents go straight to working (skipping ready) BEFORE the parent session's own turn starts, so the unpinned matcher silently bound turn_start (and everything chained off it) to a SUBAGENT's turn instead of the parent's. Fixed by pinning turn_start and pid_bind to same_session_as:session_birth (see expected.jsonl notes for the full account). Separately, the recording revealed the real session NEVER received a process_exited event at all -- the daemon's shared-PID exit watcher (processlifecycle: pidMonitor.watched map[int]string, last-write-wins per PID in monitor_darwin.go/monitor_linux.go Watch()) attributed the exit to a subagent session that happened to re-register the same OS PID more recently. This is a real, reproducible daemon race (confirmed NOT to reproduce in the sibling session-start and basic-turn recordings, where the parent session's PID gets a late re-discovery after its subagents finish, correctly re-winning the watch) -- filed as a follow-up issue (see the record subagent's issue: payload); this cell's expected.jsonl drops the redundant teardown/process_exited assertion rather than gate its own (unrelated) purpose on a bug tracked separately, since basic-turn's exit_clean-driven teardown phase already covers and reliably passes that mechanism.

sources.note: Lines 324-365 (parseRunTerminal): EventType="turn_done" on every terminal outcome. Lines 428-439 (parseAssistantMessageCommitted): PendingWaitingCue via session.ProseIndicatesWaiting over the full text. Lines 445-463 (parseAssistantToolCallsCommitted): the only path that ever populates ToolUses.

Lines 100-111 TestParseLine_RunTerminal_Completed_TurnDone; lines 245-264 TestParseLine_AssistantMessageCommitted_WaitingCue/_EmptyTextNoWaitingCue; lines 596-610 TestParseLine_TurnCompleted_RealFixture (real captured fixture, end-to-end through the tailer). Ran `go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/... -race -count=1`: all green.
Lines 569-599, IsAgentDone(): HasOpenToolCall/HasLiveBackgroundProcess veto; else HookTurnDone || LastEventType=="turn_done".
Lines 399-452, classifyAgentDone: SessionError→error; IsWaitingForUserInput()→waiting; else transitionTo(ready, "agent finished turn → ready") — rule 2b.
Lines 15-33, ProseIndicatesWaiting: OR of a trailing-question detector and an imperative-cue detector; a plain declarative final sentence trips neither.
Lines 28-37 (Source: FilesUnderRoot, static Dir, SessionIDFromPath from the session directory basename).
Lines 39-55: CommandPattern process match (muse-bin-[^/\s]+), observe-only (no hooks).

Lines 60-116 (buildAgentWatchers): the fswatcher is built from the FilesUnderRoot Dir, and a processlifecycle.Scanner (line 103) is wired unconditionally for every adapter regardless of Source variant — the mechanism a proc-<PID> presession would come from.

Lines 147-174, HasRealSessionForPID: the predicate the scanner uses to decide whether a running, process-matched PID already has a real transcript-backed session, i.e. whether to mint a proc-<PID> placeholder.

Line 139: DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean". Lines 207-212: launch-seam comment stating the session dir may only materialize after the first prompt lands. Line 235 (--trust-workspace), line 349 (sleep 0.3 before Enter), line 301 (-not -path '*/subagent/*') confirm the three previously-audited driver defects are fixed on this branch (commit 0239a1bd).

Real, redacted captured transcript slice: started → model_completed → tool call open/close → assistant_message_committed → terminal:completed — the exact end-signal shape this scenario exercises (minus the tool call, which this cell's recipe avoids).

Template for the birth-ambiguity-robust spec shape (session_birth unpinned, turn arc pinned via same_session_as turn_start) reused here for the same structural reason (a possible transient proc-<PID> presession).
Grepped all *.go files under core/pkg/capacity for "muse": zero hits — no pricing/alias entry for any muse-spark-* model, hence cost_nonzero asserted false.

preconditions: muse CLI installed and on PATH (muse --version >= 1.2.1)
auth: complete 'muse login' (Meta account, browser code approval) or export META_API_KEY
irrlichd is recording — either run-cell.sh in isolated mode, or --attach against a running daemon started with --record
setup: The interactive driver launches `muse --trust-workspace` in a fresh per-run cwd under <staging>/cwd/ via tmux, waits 1s for the TUI's input handler to finish wiring up (a live-reproduced timing requirement, not a readiness poll), then sends the prompt

Each send bumps the expected-turn counter; wait_turn resolves the driven session's own session.jsonl (excluding any subagent/ shadow) and blocks until its terminal-event count reaches the expected count

script.text: Do not use any tools. Reply with exactly this sentence and nothing else: The terminal text closes the turn.

verify: events.jsonl contains a session appearing in ready within ~2s of launch (either a proc-<PID> pre-session or the real session directly — birth shape not live-confirmed, see caveats)
events.jsonl contains a state_transition→working on the real (transcript-backed) session when the prompt is sent
events.jsonl contains a state_transition→ready on the SAME session once the terminal:completed turn closes
events.jsonl contains NO tool_use / function_call events for that session (deliberately tool-less prompt)
no state_transition→waiting appears for that session at any point (the declarative reply has no trailing question mark or imperative cue)
events.jsonl contains a pid_discovered bound to the real session
events.jsonl contains a process_exited on the real session once the driver tears the tmux session down
